items.claim: The span is one literary movement, from the year-eleven dateline at MT 30:20 to the second of two consecutive recognition refrains at MT 30:26, and every frame device the span carries is named by role: the address to the prophet at MT 30:21, the messenger formula that restates the verdict in direct divine speech at MT 30:22, and the refrains at MT 30:25 and MT 30:26. Because a refrain closes the unit before it, the later of the two refrains standing before the next dateline is this unit's close, and the onset and close evidence is strong enough on both sides to carry the high level.
items.both_sides: Onset side: MT 30:19 ends the preceding movement on a recognition refrain and the mark layer puts an open-section mark at that verse; MT 30:20 dates the oracle by year, month and day and takes the perfect word-event form. Close side: MT 30:26 ends on the recognition refrain with a closed-section mark at that verse, and MT 31:1 opens the next dated oracle, so each side of the seam carries its own evidence. Interior: the closed-section mark at MT 30:21 sits on a verse that appears in neither the recognition nor the utterance census, so it is not a refrain-grade close and cannot cut by itself; the span carries no ketiv/qere site. On the mirroring flag: the two verses argued but unmirrored, MT 30:19 and MT 31:1, are the adjacent-unit citations that assessing a seam from both sides requires, and they lie outside this span, so their absence from the span's own evidence list is correct and not a defect.

suggested_fix.fact: no change: the span, the roles assigned to each device and the level all hold on the bytes

The two interior candidates where a closed-section mark is followed by a messenger formula, MT 31:9/31:10 and MT 31:14/31:15, are refused on the operative ground, and the length disclosure with the held genre call leaves the level where the book's posture for a whole-chapter span puts it.
items.both_sides: Onset side: MT 30:26 closes the preceding unit on a recognition refrain with a closed-section mark at that verse; MT 31:1 dates this oracle by year, month and day in the perfect word-event form. Close side: MT 31:18 carries the utterance signature together with the identification of the figure as Pharaoh and a closed-section mark at that verse, and MT 32:1 opens the next dated oracle. Interior: MT 31:9 and MT 31:14 each carry a closed-section mark, but neither verse appears in the recognition census, the utterance census or the emphatic-close census, so neither is a refrain-grade close; the messenger formulae at MT 31:10 and MT 31:15 keep the same addressee and the same figure, so each marks a paragraph and neither licenses a row cut. On the mirroring flag: the unmirrored MT 30:26 and MT 32:1 are the adjacent-seam citations and lie outside this span.

items.claim: A close-grade recognition refrain stands one verse before this unit's genre colophon, at MT 32:15, and it is named nowhere in the row by any role, so the close is argued from the colophon alone when the text in fact stacks the refrain at MT 32:15 with the colophon and utterance signature at MT 32:16. The messenger sub-onsets at MT 32:3 and MT 32:11 and the utterance paragraph-closes at MT 32:8 and MT 32:14 are carried by the span and are also unnamed by role, and the alternative the row weighs is the weaker of the two candidates the span actually offers.
items.both_sides: The alternative the row does weigh is MT 32:8/32:9: on the close side MT 32:8 ends on the utterance signature, and on the onset side MT 32:9 opens a further first-person clause with no address to the prophet and no mark at the seam. The candidate left unweighed is MT 32:10/32:11: on the close side MT 32:10 carries a closed-section mark, and on the onset side MT 32:11 opens on the messenger formula, which is the same mark-then-messenger shape that is weighed and refused at MT 31:9/31:10 and MT 31:14/31:15. It fails on the same ground, because MT 32:10 appears in neither the recognition nor the utterance census, so the mark sits on a verse that carries no refrain-grade close, and the addressee does not change across it. Against both candidates stands the text's own bracketing: the lament word in the command at MT 32:2 and the colophon at MT 32:16 label the unit at its two ends, and a unit the text labels this way is not cut on an interior formula recurrence. So the span keeps and the high level stands; what is deficient is the disclosure and the choice of rejected alternative. On the mirroring flag: the unmirrored MT 31:18 and MT 32:17 are the adjacent-seam citations and lie outside this span.

suggested_fix.fact: a recognition refrain stands immediately before the colophon, so this unit's close is a stacked refrain and colophon rather than a colophon alone; and the two messenger sub-onsets and two utterance paragraph-closes inside the span are devices this unit carries, the second messenger formula standing on the far side of the span's own closed-section mark

items.claim: The onset gloss gives MT 32:17 a month that neither witness carries. MT 32:17 dates the oracle by a year and by a day of the month with no month term at all, and the translation reads the same way, while MT 32:1 names its month explicitly; the half-month interval the row asserts between this onset and the preceding dated oracle rests on that supplied month and is not derivable from either witness. The dateline itself is sound, since a year word together with a day term is what the dateline category requires, so the defect is in the gloss and the interval drawn from it, not in the seam.
items.both_sides: Onset side: MT 32:16 closes the preceding unit on its genre colophon with the utterance signature and an open-section mark at that verse; MT 32:17 is a year-bearing dateline in the perfect word-event form, followed by the command to the prophet at MT 32:18, so the seam stands whatever is decided about the month. Close side: MT 32:32 carries the second of two consecutive utterance signatures, MT 32:31 the first, with an open-section mark at MT 32:32, which is this collection's own close and the strongest close-side evidence in the cluster. Interior: the roster from MT 32:22 to MT 32:30 is a refrain list and is not cut inside, the span carries no messenger formula at all, and the paseq at MT 32:24 is count-only, so no interior candidate arises. On the mirroring flag: the sixteen verses argued but unmirrored are the whole preceding unit cited as a range, and the genre contrast the row draws rests on exactly two of them, the lament word in the opening command and the same word in the colophon, so a two-verse anchor carries the identical argument with fourteen fewer unmirrored references.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The level on the Sheol-roster unit at Ezek.32.17-Ezek.32.32 is the lowest in the cluster, while its boundary evidence is the strongest: a year-bearing dateline onset with an open-section mark and a genre colophon behind it, and a doubled utterance close with an open-section mark that is also this collection's own close. The row's own reasoning ties the level to the held genre call rather than to the boundaries, and the eighteen-verse cedar unit at Ezek.31.1-Ezek.31.18, whose genre call is held in the same way, sits a step higher.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: A consumer cannot tell whether the number reports boundary strength or genre certainty, and the two adjacent units answer that question differently. Whether the level should track the form evidence for the seams, with the genre hold disclosed separately, is a calibration question this lens can raise from the bytes but cannot settle alone.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The length disclosure on the cedar unit at Ezek.31.1-Ezek.31.18 measures itself against the fourteen-to-sixteen verse allowance, which the ruled granularity grants to measured and listed blocks; this unit is neither, and the ruled target density for an ordinary formula-bounded unit is lower.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: The disclosure is conservative rather than wrong, since it names the most permissive ceiling and still reports exceeding it, and the mechanical cap arm reads green either way. But the benchmark named is not the one that governs this unit, and a later reader checking the length rule against this row would be pointed at the wrong allowance.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether the cure for the month at Ezek.32.17 should state that the witnesses name no month, or simply omit the month from the gloss, is a convention question and not a factual one.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: Both forms remove the false component, but only the first leaves a reader able to see why the interval between this dated oracle and the preceding one is not stated. The other dated oracles in this cluster do carry a month, so silence here would read as an omission rather than as a property of the text.
